fields.description:
## Context / Problem

Daily plan-review cache reads in `.rebar/usage.jsonl` went from ~80% of input tokens (2026-08-06..11) to 0 from 2026-08-12 onward, and the median full plan review went from about $2.18 to about $4.82 (Aug 6–29 logged spend is roughly $3,000). The change coincides with commit `6d4f394195b2` (2026-08-10, ticket `esthetical-earthborn-vervet` / `8fbd-e9d5-326e-40d8`) adding the Anthropic-direct fallback to the frontier/standard classes in `rebar.toml` `[llm.model_classes]`. `_intersect_capabilities` in `src/rebar/llm/runner_support.py` intersects capabilities across the whole chain and collapses differing `prompt_cache_style` values to `"none"`, so every call on a mixed chain runs uncached even though the primary Bedrock target supports caching.

Both mixed chains are **Bedrock-primary, Anthropic-fallback** (`rebar.toml:223-224`): `frontier = bedrock:...opus + fallback anthropic:...opus`; `standard` likewise for sonnet. The Anthropic hedge fires **0.43%** of calls (empirical: 51 of 11,902 logged rows), so the collapse disables caching on the Bedrock target that serves ~99.6% of calls.

## Prior art this reverses, and why reversing is sound

The whole-chain collapse-to-none is documented/approved intent, recorded in THREE places, and this fix updates all three:

1. The `_intersect_capabilities` **docstring** (`runner_support.py:56-58`) — this is where the founding PREMISE lives: each style's cache keys are provider-specific and "would error on the candidate that does not share it," so a mixed chain must fail closed.
2. The `rebar.toml` `[llm.model_classes]` note (~190-193) — "Mixed-provider chains disable prompt caching because their provider-specific cache keys do not intersect."
3. `docs/llm-framework.md` (~829-840) — names `_intersect_capabilities` as "the authority" and restates the collapse-to-none intent.

ADR 0059 §7 does NOT assert that premise; it documents the per-provider cache-key mechanics (`bedrock_cache_*` vs `anthropic_cache_*`), the shared-automatic-key rejection (LangChain#37042), and per-model floors. It gets a superseding note so its recorded architecture matches, and its §2 invariant (capability decisions read a ModelProfile/capability FIELD, never a provider-name string) is preserved.

**The founding premise is false for cache keys, proven at runtime against the pinned pydantic-ai:**

- The cache directive is a set of provider-scoped `ModelSettings` keys (`capabilities.py:664-716`). `ModelSettings` is a `TypedDict(total=False)` — no runtime key validation — and `pydantic_ai.settings.merge_model_settings` is a plain dict union (`base | overrides`), also no validation.
- Each provider model reads ONLY its own keys via `model_settings.get('<prefix>_cache_*')`. `AnthropicModel` consults exactly four keys (`anthropic.py:1190,1580,1719,1766`); a `bedrock_cache_*` key is a silent `.get()` miss. So when the rare Anthropic fallback actually serves the Bedrock-primary directive, it applies NO caching, adds NO top-level `cache_control`, and cannot reach the `anthropic_cache`/`anthropic_cache_messages` mutual-exclusion `UserError`: **uncached-but-correct, never an error** (runtime-verified; mirrors LiteLLM, which "silently skips" an inapplicable cache directive with "no error").
- The "Bedrock rejects a top-level `cache_control`" wire error (ADR 0059 §7; **LangChain#37042**) is the OPPOSITE case: produced only by `anthropic_cache=True` (Anthropic's automatic top-level key) reaching a Bedrock model — i.e. an Anthropic-PRIMARY chain. No chain in `rebar.toml` is Anthropic-primary, and even if one were, a Bedrock model never reads `anthropic_cache`, so the top-level `cache_control` is never emitted for it. LangChain#37042 argues FOR per-resolved-provider cache keys (which rebar already emits) and AGAINST a shared/automatic key — it does not support a chain-wide capability collapse.

The asymmetry, therefore: fields that CAN hard-fail cross-provider (`supports_temperature` → HTTP 400, `native_structured_output`, `supports_thinking`, `native_output_with_thinking`, `native_web_search`) STILL fail closed with `all(...)`; only `prompt_cache_style` — advisory and inert cross-provider — follows the PRIMARY. This aligns rebar with pydantic-ai's own model (`FallbackModel` re-prepares settings per resolved candidate) and LiteLLM's (caching is a property of the resolved serving model, `supports_prompt_caching(model=…)`), not a min-intersection across candidates.

## Approach

Option **(a): fix the capability seam** (operator decision; option (b) — homogenising the chains — is OFF THE TABLE because the Anthropic hedge is required functionality). In `_intersect_capabilities`, derive `prompt_cache_style` from `per_candidate[0]` (the primary/serving candidate) instead of collapsing to `"none"` on disagreement; keep every hard-failing field conservatively `all(...)`-intersected. Update the now-stale documented intent in the three sites above to match. The runtime safety analysis establishes (a) does NOT destabilise the seam, so no escalation.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/runner_support.py` — the seam fix + docstring rewrite (this is site 1 of the stale intent).
- `tests/unit/test_runner_support.py` — NEW focused module for `_intersect_capabilities`. The function is defined in `runner_support.py`, so a `test_runner_support.py` module is the natural home; `tests/unit/test_llm_capabilities.py` imports the function via the `rebar.llm.runner` re-export but asserts native-output-under-thinking behavior, which this change leaves intact (verified still-green). The new module holds the cache-follows-primary regression + the fallback-fires safety proof so the reversed behavior has a single, discoverable coverage site.
- `rebar.toml` — update the `[llm.model_classes]` caching comment (site 2).
- `docs/adr/0059-llm-provider-seam-and-support-tiers.md` — superseding decision note in §7.
- `docs/llm-framework.md` — update the mixed-provider-chain caching stanza (site 3).

## Testing

Unit (`tests/unit/test_runner_support.py`):
- Mixed Bedrock-primary + Anthropic-fallback chain keeps the primary's `"bedrock"` cache style (core regression; RED before the fix).
- Symmetry: an Anthropic-primary chain keeps `"anthropic"`; a `"none"`-primary chain stays `"none"`; a homogeneous chain is unchanged.
- Hard-fail fields (`supports_temperature`, `native_structured_output`) STILL intersect conservatively on a mixed chain (guards against over-broadening).
- **Fallback-actually-fires safety** (parametrized single + agentic): `cache_settings_for` on the mixed chain emits only `bedrock_cache_*` keys, and merging them into the Anthropic arm's settings leaves every `anthropic_cache_*` read `None` and the mutual-exclusion `UserError` unreachable — codifying the ignored-not-errored proof for the branch where the Anthropic fallback serves.

Mutation-checked: seeding the exact historical collapse-to-none defect turns 5 of the 7 tests RED (the two `"none"`/homogeneous controls stay green either way).

Live check: one `review-plan` after the fix shows `cache_read_tokens > 0` on second and later finder calls in `.rebar/usage.jsonl`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A regression test proves a mixed Bedrock-primary chain reports `prompt_cache_style == "bedrock"` (not `"none"`); RED before the fix, green after; runs in `make test`.
- [ ] A test proves the fallback-serves branch is safe: the primary cache directive is inert on the Anthropic arm (every `anthropic_cache_*` read is `None`, no `UserError`), so a served fallback runs uncached-but-correct.
- [ ] Hard-fail capability fields remain `all(...)`-intersected on a mixed chain (a regression test asserts `supports_temperature`/`native_structured_output` still withdraw).
- [ ] All three stale-intent sites are updated to cache-follows-primary: the `_intersect_capabilities` docstring, `rebar.toml` (~190-193), `docs/llm-framework.md` (~829-840); and ADR 0059 §7 carries a superseding note.
- [ ] After the fix, a production plan review logs non-zero `cache_read_tokens` in `.rebar/usage.jsonl`.
- [ ] The root cause, prior-art engagement, and the chosen option are recorded on this ticket.
